1. (Currently Amended) A method, comprising: inputting database constructs generated by a database optimizer as an input to a trained machine-learning algorithm that has been trained on historical database performance data; obtaining a database operation predictor from the machine-learning algorithm as an output, wherein the database operation predictor comprises a predicted performance metric not previously calculated by the database optimizer; modifying at least one of the database constructs based on the database operation predictor producing a modified database construct that differs from any database construct produced by the database optimizer; and processing a database operation with the database constructs and the modified database construct.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein inputting further includes inputting the database constructs as query execution plans for a query, and wherein the trained machine-learning algorithm receives as input features derived from the query execution plans that are distinct from cost metrics generated by the database optimizer.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein inputting further includes identifying at least one database construct as a least cost query execution plan identified from the query execution plans by the database optimizer, and wherein the machine-learning algorithm generates a predicted performance metric that is independent of the cost identification process of the database optimizer.

4. (Previously presented) The method of claim 3, wherein identifying further includes identifying individual pieces of the least cost query execution plan as: a total number of spools used, cardinality for tables with any intermediate results used, a total number of merge joins, a total number of hash joins, nested loop joins, references for the spools, and costs per database resource assigned by the database optimizer.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated Central Process Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation, wherein the estimated CPU execution time is predicted by the machine-learning algorithm based on patterns in historical execution data rather than derived from optimizer cost models.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation, wherein the estimated number of I/O operations is predicted by the machine-learning algorithm based on patterns in historical execution data rather than derived from optimizer cost models.

7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for the database operation as the modified database construct, wherein the scheduled execution time is adjusted based on the predicted performance metric to achieve a performance objective not achievable using the database constructs alone.

8. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for execution of a query as the modified database construct, wherein the scheduled execution time is adjusted based on the predicted performance metric to achieve a performance objective not achievable using the database constructs alone.

9. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a workgroup assigned to the database operation as the modified database construct, wherein the workgroup assignment is changed based on the predicted performance metric to optimize resource utilization in a manner not determined by the database optimizer.

10. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising, storing the database operation predictor in database statistics associated with the database operation and the database constructs, wherein the database operation predictor is stored separately from cost metrics generated by the database optimizer.

11. (Original) The method of claim 10 further comprising, rendering an interface from the database statistics depicting relationships between the database operation, the database operation predictor, the database constructs, and the modified database construct with respect to other instances of the database operation, other database operation predictors, other database constructs, and other modified database constructs.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: training a machine-learning algorithm with database constructs produced by a database optimizer, wherein the training uses historical actual execution performance data that is distinct from cost estimates generated by the database optimizer; receiving query execution plans for a query from the database optimizer with a least cost query execution plan identified by the database optimizer for the query; providing the query execution plans as input to the machine-learning algorithm; obtaining as an output a predicted execution time for the query based on the least cost query execution plan, wherein the predicted execution time is generated by the machine-learning algorithm and is independent of the optimizer's cost estimation; and modifying one of: the least cost query execution plan for the query, a scheduled execution time for the query, and resources that are used to execute the query based on the predicted execution time, wherein the modification is made to achieve a performance objective not achievable using the least cost query execution plan alone.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising, notifying a database administrator when based on the predicted execution time a Service Level Goal (SLG) or Service Level Agreement (SLA) associated with the query will be unable to be satisfied using the least cost query execution plan or using a modified version of the least cost query execution plan that was modified based on the predicted execution time.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising: providing an interface rendered through a database tool that models the database constructs, the query execution plans, an actual query execution time for the query, and the predicted execution time for the query against other queries having other database constructs, other query execution plans, other actual query execution times for the other queries, and other predicted execution times provided by the machine-learning algorithm for the other queries.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein providing further includes providing the database tool within a workload scheduler and management component of a database system.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein training further includes training the machine-learning algorithm as a linear regression-based machine-learning algorithm using historical actual execution performance data that is distinct from cost estimates generated by the database optimizer.

17. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes selecting a different one of the query execution plans to execute the query instead of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted execution time and a historical actual execution time known for the different query execution plan.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes changing an execution resource of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted query execution time and a current performance associated with the execution resource, wherein the change is determined by the machine-learning algorithm based on predicted performance metrics rather than by the database optimizer's cost estimation.

19. (Currently Amended) A system, comprising: a database management system; at least one hardware processor; a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having executable instructions representing a trained machine-learning algorithm that has been trained on historical database performance data; the machine learning algorithm configured to execute on the at least one hardware processor from the non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and to perform processing to: i) receive as input database constructs produced by a database optimizer for a database operation of the database management system; and ii) provide as output a predicted value relevant to one of: one or more of the database constructs and the database operation, wherein the predicted value is generated by the machine-learning algorithm based on patterns in historical execution data and is independent of cost metrics generated by the database optimizer; wherein the database management system is configured to process the predicted value to determine whether to modify one of: the one or more database constructs and the database operation before processing the database operation within the database management system, wherein the modification is made to achieve a performance objective not achievable using the database constructs alone.

20. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 19, wherein the predicted value is an estimated query execution time for a query predicted by the machine-learning algorithm based on historical execution patterns, and the database operation is execution of a query execution plan for the query within the database management system, wherein the estimated query execution time is independent of cost estimates generated by the database optimizer.
